content.comment_body: I developed an FBD program using [product_name] V8, utilizing 318 function blocks and reaching a layout memory size of 79867 bytes. The simulation worked as intended. After upgrading to [product_name] V8.2, I opened and simulated the same program without issues. However, when attempting to download this program to the [product_name] hardware ([version_no], FS 06) via [product_name] V8.2, I encountered a problem: the info window displayed a download failure, and the program could not be transferred to the device. I realize my memory usage exceeds 30000 bytes, which causes lines to get mixed after uploading, but I do not understand why downloading fails outright, especially since simulation works as expected.

Thread closed since the same question was posted more than once. The second thread titled 'Download program to [product_name] hardware by [product_name] V8.2' is now published in the relevant conference section. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user is unable to transfer a large FBD program designed and successfully simulated in [product_name] V8.2 to a [product_name] hardware ([version_no], FS 06), encountering a download failure without clear error details. Although the user is aware that the memory usage greatly exceeds official guidelines, it is unclear why this blocks the download process while simulation remains successful.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to download and operate a large, simulated program on their [product_name] hardware, even when it surpasses suggested memory limits. Clear information about download restrictions and failure reasons is sought.
